messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: control-plane › auth-dep — elevated 5xx rate detected (502/504/timeouts) beginning ~12:13 UTC. Service: auth-lookup (org-lookup path). Current error rate: ~18% across control-plane requests. Paging oncall: @Aisha. Runbook: https://redwood.infra/runbooks/auth-dep-5xx
Aisha: ack - I'm oncall. Looking at dashboards now. Can someone drop the traces and recent deploys?
Miguel: I see a config rollout to org-lookup cache TTL that completed ~12:05 UTC across regions. Traffic/latency correlate. Logs show internal lookup timeouts to kv-cache.
Ravi: adding SRE thread - preliminary hypothesis: TTL change caused stampede on backend KV causing timeouts -> 5xx bubbled up. Reproducing errors in staging now.
Zoe: product note: Partner integrations showing spike in failed logins (oauth flows). Customer impact: several mid-market customers reporting auth timeouts in support. Priya, can you surface names?
Priya: yep — ticket stream shows customers: AcmeCorp, BrightAds, and two enterprise sandboxes. I'm prepping an incident message for affected customers if we hit mitigation rollback.
Aisha: mitigation plan (quick):
- 1) Revert config rollout to previous TTL (fast rollback)
- 2) Route auth traffic to fallback cluster (replica with older cache behavior) using routing policy
- 3) Temporarily increase upstream timeouts from 2s -> 5s
- 4) Disable full org-lookup for non-critical paths (soft degrade)
Who can trigger the rollback and routing change?
Miguel: I can do the rollback and route. Rollback command is in deploy-runbook. Running pre-checks.
Miguel: log snippet showing KV errors:
```
ERROR auth-lookup kv-client.go:172: get(key="org:1234") -> upstream timeout after 2000ms
WARN circuitbreaker: open for kv-primary (error-rate 38%)
```
Ravi: also seeing backend saturation on read replicas. We should throttle burst callers and enable small jitter to avoid thundering herd.
Aisha: execute rollback + route then report status. Keep config change window short.
Miguel: initiating rollback now (deploy-runbook step 3). Command:
```
./deployctl rollback --service auth-config --to "2026-03-14T11:50:22Z"
```
deploy-bot: rollback started for auth-config by Miguel at 12:29 UTC. 3/3 regions acknowledged.
Miguel: rollback completed. Verifying metrics.
Aisha: rebooting routing policy to prefer fallback cluster for org-lookup paths.
Miguel: routed ~40% of traffic to fallback cluster, then 100% after 2m. Initial error rate dropped from 18% -> 3% within 90s.
Priya: support update: acknowledging reduction in error rates; customers are still seeing intermittent 502s but improving. Drafting customer comms: "We've mitigated an auth dependency issue affecting logins; rollback applied; monitoring."
Zoe: product request: keep org-lookup degraded flag until we confirm stability for 30m and then can re-enable gradually with canary.
Ravi: telemetry shows backend KV error-rate trending down. Circuit breaker metrics: failures-> 5% now. But we should also patch the cache stampede at root (rate limiting + warmed cache priming).
Aisha: action items captured:
- Miguel: follow-up postmortem + hotfix for TTL rollout gating and deploy checks (ETA 2h)
- Ravi: add auto-throttle and jitter to cache priming logic (ETA 4h)
- Priya & Zoe: customer comms & impacted customer list (today)
- Aisha: monitor 30m, then handoff to night oncall with summary
Miguel: opening a ticket: INF-71234 with rollback timeline, deploy diff, and logs.
Priya: bumped support tickets and informed account teams for AcmeCorp + BrightAds.
Aisha: current status: mitigated (error rate normalized to baseline). Will keep flags in place for 30m. Preparing handoff for 20:00 UTC. Next oncall: Miguel.
Miguel: I will take handoff at 20:00 UTC. I'll watch graphs and follow through on the hotfix ticket.
deploy-bot: incident tag applied to rollback deploy (deploy-id: dpl-8891).
Aisha: handoff summary for next oncall (Miguel) — root cause likely KV stampede from TTL change in org-lookup cache during rollout. Mitigation: rollback + route to fallback cluster + increased timeouts + temporary degradation of org-lookup. Customer impact: intermittent login failures for select customers; now improving. See INF-71234 for details. If errors recur, escalate to EngRuntime and SRE. :white_check_mark:
Miguel: acked. I'll pick this up and keep monitoring. If we see >5% error rate for 5m, I'll page and escalate.
